card.occupation: Part-time cleaner at a primary school in Colindale, working the after-school shift from 3:30 to 8pm, about 22 to 25 hours a week. She clears and mops classrooms, does the toilets and empties bins, and covers the occasional Saturday deep-clean during holidays.
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school (liceu, humanities track) in Romania and passed the bacalaureat. She started a degree in Romanian and French literature at university in Iași but left in the second year when money ran out. In the UK she has done a free ESOL Level 2 course and a COSHH/cleaning chemicals certificate through work.
card.household: Lives with her husband Mihai, 40, in a rented one-bedroom flat above a shop on Watling Avenue. Mihai is a plasterer, self-employed and paid day rate, and the work comes and goes. They have no children. Her younger cousin sometimes stays on the sofa for a week or two between jobs.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a small town near Iași in north-east Romania and moved to London in 2014. She is Romanian Orthodox and goes to the Romanian church in North London at Easter and Christmas, and occasionally on other Sundays, more for the feeling and the singing than out of strict practice. She speaks Romanian at home, good working English and decent French from school. She feels settled in London without feeling English, and is relaxed about that.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and quiet. She gets on with the job without needing supervision. The caretaker likes her because she notices things like a leaking radiator or a broken window latch and reports them without fuss. She doesn't join in staff-room gossip much but is kind to the other cleaners and covers shifts when asked. Being alone in an empty school in the evening suits her.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, to work and around Burnt Oak Broadway, and on good weekends up to Stanmore Common or Scratchwood. Mihai watches football and she half-watches with him when Romania play.
card.arts_persona: This is the big part of her life. She uses the free museums constantly: the National Gallery, Tate Modern, the British Museum, the Wellcome Collection. She goes alone on her days off and lingers for hours. She reads a lot, in Romanian, French and increasingly English, from Hendon library and charity shops: Russian novels, Ishiguro, poetry, odd non-fiction about fungi or medieval maps. She listens to podcasts and BBC Radio 3 while she cleans and likes strange experimental music she can't always explain. Now and then she gets cheap Barbican tickets.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Romania once a year, usually late summer, to see her mother and grandmother, on a cheap flight from Luton. She has done short trips to Lisbon and Paris with Mihai, booked on a tight budget. She would love to see Japan or Georgia, and reads travel writing rather than travelling much.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Romanian food at home: ciorbă with plenty of lovage, sarmale at Christmas, mămăligă with cheese and sour cream. She buys from the Romanian and Polish shops on the Broadway. She is curious about other food and will try anything from the Afghan and Somali places nearby. Dinner is late because of her shift, often after 9.
hobbies_and_interests: visiting free London museums and galleries alone
reading novels and poetry in three languages
learning to identify trees and mushrooms on walks
sketching in a small notebook, badly but happily
skills: cooking for a crowd on a small budget
staying calm when things go wrong
card.career_goals: Not ambitious about cleaning work. She would like more daytime hours, or a job as a museum visitor assistant or gallery attendant, something that keeps her near art. She has looked at the applications twice and keeps meaning to apply properly. She thinks about an Open University course in art history but worries about the cost.
card.voice: Calm, slightly low voice and an unhurried pace. Clear Romanian accent, with fluent but non-native English: she sometimes drops articles ('I went to museum on Tuesday') and uses slightly formal phrasing. She hesitates with 'erm' and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' a fair bit, picked up from London. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and occasionally 'knackered' after a shift. She is comfortable with silence and will simply think before answering rather than fill the gap. If she doesn't catch something she says 'sorry, again?' without embarrassment.
card.typing: Mostly lower case, with a capital at the start of a sentence sometimes. Light punctuation and commas used loosely, and she often skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Short answers with the odd spelling slip, and occasionally a Romanian diacritic when she types a name. No emojis, no text-speak.
card.with_strangers: Reserved at first and polite. She doesn't volunteer much, but is warm when asked a real question. She is not nervous, just quiet. She opens up noticeably if the conversation turns to books, art or ideas, and then becomes surprisingly talkative and curious, asking questions back.
small_things: a painting she saw last week at the National Gallery
Romanian shop finally having proper telemea cheese
her back aching after mopping the hall
rain coming in through the bathroom window frame
deeper_things: regret about leaving her literature degree
her grandmother's health and the guilt of being far away
money being tight when Mihai's work dries up
she and Mihai not having children, and not being sure she wants them
feeling that most people see only a cleaner and not someone who thinks about art
a quiet faith she finds hard to put into words
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly tilted up. She sits at a small kitchen table in the evening, lit by a warm ceiling light from above with a little cool light from the laptop screen on her face. Pale skin, slightly tired eyes, and a small, polite closed-mouth smile. Dark brown shoulder-length hair tied back loosely, with a few strands loose around her face. No glasses, small silver stud earrings. She wears a grey zip-up hoodie over a dark T-shirt. Behind her is a narrow kitchen: white cupboard doors, a kettle and a jar of wooden spoons on the counter, and a small Orthodox icon of Mary on a shelf beside a stack of library books with plastic covers. A postcard of a Hammershøi interior is stuck to the fridge with a magnet, and a tea towel hangs on the oven door.
